seo.title: FLUX 3 Video Draft Generator for 720p Iteration
seo.description: Use FLUX 3 Video Draft for 720p text, image, first-last-frame and extension trials, with exact source rules, prompt guidance and mode-aware quotes.

overview: FLUX 3 Video Draft is the current 720p iteration sibling in the FLUX video family. It mirrors the four launch workflows while returning a draft-oriented result and cache context. Black Forest Labs owns the model; MaxVideoAI distributes these endpoints through Fal. Draft is positioned for testing, not as an automatic substitute for standard FLUX 3 production review.

hero.title: FLUX 3 Video Draft
hero.subtitle: Test text, opening-image, first-and-last-frame and source-video extension ideas at the fixed 720p draft tier.
hero.paragraph: Choose Draft while comparing scene direction, source compatibility and transition logic before a standard FLUX 3 pass. First-and-last-frame still requires both anchors, and extension still requires a source video with its own mode-specific quote. Black Forest Labs owns FLUX and Fal distributes execution for this MaxVideoAI launch.

features.title: Fixed 720p iteration
features.body: Draft has one supported output tier, which makes it useful for direction tests without pretending to offer the standard model's 1080p option. Choose the sibling after a concept survives review.

features.title: Same explicit source roles
features.body: Text needs a prompt, image mode needs an opening image, fl2v needs both start and end images, and extension needs a video. Draft does not relax those required inputs.

features.title: Fast creative decisions
features.body: Use short controlled scenes to compare camera direction, action timing and visual continuity. Avoid spending the draft loop on several unrelated story beats that cannot be diagnosed.

features.title: Draft extension remains separate
features.body: Extension uses a distinct canonical pricing rule even on Draft. The page sends mode extend into the calculator rather than presenting a normal-generation estimate.

decisionCards.title: Best fit: controlled 720p trials
decisionCards.body: Use Draft for early frame bridges, source-video continuation tests, motion sketches and prompt comparisons with one measurable change per attempt.

decisionCards.title: Not ideal: final production equivalence
decisionCards.body: Draft is not described as equivalent to standard FLUX 3 delivery. Move the selected concept to the standard sibling when the production brief calls for that route or 1080p.

decisionCards.title: Design tests that transfer
decisionCards.body: Keep source frames, prompt structure and acceptance criteria reusable so the successful draft can be evaluated consistently on the standard model.

tabNotes.body: A draft is valuable when it reduces one concrete uncertainty, even if it is not a final asset.
The Draft contract does not turn fl2v into arbitrary keyframes or make the end image optional.
Record sources, prompt and acceptance notes before switching to standard FLUX 3.

globalPrinciples: Change one major variable per draft.
Use sources that are compatible in identity and scene logic.
Keep movement physically readable at short duration.
Apply rights, consent and safety review even to temporary outputs.
engineWhy: A fixed 720p route keeps Draft positioning clear.
Four explicit modes let teams test the same source contracts before production handoff.
Separate extension pricing prevents a draft continuation from being quoted as ordinary generation.

demo.title: FLUX 3 Draft continuation test
demo.prompt: Continue the supplied clip from its final frame: the small research boat keeps moving left to right through low morning fog while the camera maintains the same slow aerial track. A buoy passes beneath the frame and the wake widens naturally. Preserve hull colors, crew count, horizon height and cool light. Do not introduce a cut, title, logo or new vessel.
notes: The prompt begins from the source clip's ending state.
Continuity anchors make the draft useful for standard-model handoff.
